fix: Option::map is used only for its side effect in every arm, so each arm yields an unused Option<()>. Write the arms as statements, e.g. `GestureAction::Tap => { if let Some(callback) = &self.callbacks.on_tap { callback(); } }`, or use a small private helper `fn call_unit(cb: &Option<Box<dyn Fn()>>)` to keep the match compact. Keep the same callback order and the LongPressStart arm's start-then-long-press sequence.

The comment's claim is wrong: `Any::type_id` can be called on the `&mut dyn Any` returned by as_any_mut, and virtual dispatch yields the concrete type's TypeId. Compute the real id before the downcast, e.g. `let actual = (*recognizer.as_any_mut()).type_id();` (dyn Any receiver, no 'static borrow issue), then use `actual` in the Err arm and delete the misleading comment. Verify with a test in crates/incular-gestures/tests/ that a mismatched factory reports the concrete recognizer TypeId.
